Search returns nothing, but I have read the entire document. Assessment:

**Vendor indemnity (§10(a), p0047–p0051):** Kubient defends, indemnifies and holds harmless AP and its officers/directors/agents/employees against **all** third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and Kubient's (or its subcontractors') acts or omissions. Because §9(b)(i) warrants the Service and deliverables do not "infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party," and §9(b)(iii)/(ix) warrant data security and legal compliance, the indemnity reaches IP infringement, Vendor data breach, breach of law, and negligence/misconduct. No Customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs and **no super-cap** — both better than fallback.

**Procedure (§11, p0053–p0055):** notice, indemnitor control of defence (with consent for liability-admitting settlements), and reasonable cooperation at the indemnitor's cost — all three preferred procedure elements present.

Shortfalls are sub-preferred only: "affiliates" not named (though officers/directors/agents/employees are), no procure/modify/replace/refund ladder, and AP's §10(b) indemnity is broader than "Customer content plus breach of law." None is a walk-away or fallback failure, and adding the fallback's 3× super-cap would weaken us.

input.rationale: Section 10(a) gives us an express Kubient duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless AP and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees against all third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors. Read with the §9(b) warranties, that reaches third-party IP infringement (9(b)(i): the Service and deliverables "do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party"), Vendor-caused data/security failures (9(b)(iii)), and Kubient's breach of applicable Law (9(b)(ix)), with negligence and wilful misconduct captured by the "acts or omissions of Kubient" limb. Section 11 supplies the full standard procedure: prompt written notice (without forfeiture for delay), indemnitor control of defence and settlement subject to our consent for any settlement admitting our liability, and reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and substantially meets the preferred position, and it is materially better than fallback in two respects that favour us: there are no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, and Kubient's indemnity is not subject to any super-cap (§7(a) also carves indemnification out of the damages exclusion). We note three sub-preferred points for the record rather than redlining them: "affiliates" are not named as indemnified parties (officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees are); there is no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder; and AP's reciprocal §10(b) indemnity is broader than the preferred "Customer content and Customer's breach of law," extending to unauthorized use of the Services/Platform and AP's acts or omissions. None of these is a walk-away or a material fallback failure, and proposing the fallback's 3x annual-fee super-cap would weaken our current uncapped recourse, so we do not redline.
